name: Sly and Robbie
hook: Jamaica's most recorded rhythm section, who took the dub studio's logic of drum and bass as the song into reggae, pop, and hip-hop sessions worldwide.

blurb.age7: A drummer and a bass player who played together so often and so well that people just called them one name.
blurb.age13: Drummer Sly Dunbar and bassist Robbie Shakespeare started playing together at Channel One studio in Kingston in 1975. As the in-house band, they built new drum-and-bass patterns on hundreds of records, then took that sound out of Jamaica and onto records by Black Uhuru, Grace Jones, and many others.
blurb.adult: Dunbar and Shakespeare were the house rhythm section at Channel One from 1975, developing patterns that shifted reggae away from rocksteady toward the more mechanical, bass-forward feel that dub had been pointing toward. Their move to Chris Blackwell's Compass Point Studios in Nassau put them at the center of early-1980s crossover pop production, applying the same rhythm logic to a much wider range of artists.

signatureTracks.title: Sinsemilla (Black Uhuru)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The rhythm section at its most influential, driving Black Uhuru toward an international audience.

signatureTracks.title: Language Barrier
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Recorded with Bill Laswell in New York, this is Sly and Robbie stepping out from behind other artists to make the record under their own name.
